method: Stratified hand-verification of claim-level faithfulness verdicts. Each sampled verdict was read against the full text of the chunk the judge was shown. Adjudicated by the human-in-the-loop reviewer, not by another model. Sample drawn by evaluation/verify_judge.py --n 6 --pin Mexico,Japan --seed 20260719.
why_stratified: Sampling only suspicious (UNSUPPORTED) verdicts would measure false-rejection rate and say nothing about rubber-stamping. The two error directions bias the headline in OPPOSITE ways, so accuracy is reported per direction and never blended.

unsupported_direction.interpretation: The judge OVER-REJECTS. Both errors were over-strict readings of chunks that a human would accept. This means the headline faithfulness is UNDERSTATED, not inflated.

verdicts.claim: As a US citizen, you do not need a visa to visit Japan for a stay of up to 90 days
verdicts.note: Cited chunk [4] covers transit-without-visa, Shore Pass and Residence Card. It never states US citizens are visa-exempt. The CLAIM IS TRUE and the corpus does support it elsewhere (state_dept idx=0: 'No visa required for stays less than 90 days') -- but the model cited the wrong chunk. Correct answer, wrong citation: exactly the attribution failure this metric exists to catch.

verdicts.claim: US citizens do not need a visa to visit Mexico for stays of up to 180 days
verdicts.note: Cited chunk [1] is the Travel Advisory page header -- 'Skip to content', 'Worldwide Caution', advisory-level boilerplate. Zero visa content. Again the claim is true and the corpus states it at state_dept idx=13 ('A visa is required when visiting for more than 180 days'), but that chunk was not the one cited.

verdicts.claim: These areas provide a mix of modern architecture, shopping, dining, and cultural experiences
verdicts.note: Cited chunk is a bare district-name list (Al Seef, Al Quoz, Business Bay...) with no descriptions whatsoever. The characterisation is invented. Same defect flagged in Phase 1d.

verdicts.claim: Äscher Cliff Restaurant provides unique dining experience with stunning views
verdicts.note: Chunk contains only the heading 'Hiking and Äscher cliff restaurant'. 'Unique dining experience with stunning views' is fabricated embellishment.

verdicts.claim: Alpstein Area is a destination for hiking and exploring
verdicts.note: JUDGE WRONG (over-strict). The chunk's section heading is literally 'Hiking and Äscher cliff restaurant', immediately followed by the Alpstein description. A human reads that as supporting 'Alpstein is for hiking'. Borderline, but the support is present.

verdicts.claim: It is generally safe to travel in Norway right now
verdicts.note: JUDGE WRONG (over-strict). Cited chunks carry CDC 'Level 1 Practice Usual Precautions' and State Dept Level 1. Level 1 is the standard institutional signal for 'safe'; requiring the literal word 'safe' is too literal a reading.

supported_direction.interpretation: No rubber-stamping detected. Every sampled approval was traceable to near-verbatim chunk text.

verdicts.claim: All international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with MMR
verdicts.note: Chunk states it verbatim: 'All international travelers should be fully vaccinated against measles with the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine'.

verdicts.claim: Routine vaccinations: Varicella, DTaP/Tdap/Td, Flu, MMR, Polio, Shingles
verdicts.note: Matches the CDC routine-vaccine block present in the cited CDC chunk.

MY OWN CHECK WAS WRONG FIRST. Grepping the cited chunks for 'Rhodes' returned nothing, which looked like a rubber-stamp. But the chunk reads '(Ρόδος, Ródos) — island with ancient monuments, as well as beaches'. Ródos IS Rhodes. The judge was right and my verification instrument was too literal. Root cause: the cleaner deleted the English name 'Rhodes' (and 'Crete', 'Athens', 'Corfu', 'Mykonos') as repeated short lines, leaving only Greek script and transliteration.

verdicts.claim: Massachusetts road trip through Boston, Cape Cod and the Berkshires
verdicts.note: Chunk: 'Plan a Massachusetts road trip through Boston, Cape Cod, Central Massachusetts and the Berkshires, exploring history, coastline and scenic stops'. Near-verbatim.

verdicts.claim: Yulong Snow Mountain is known for its sacred summit of snow and ice
verdicts.note: Chunk: 'Yulong Snow Mountain: the sacred summit of snow and ice'. Verbatim.

verdicts.claim: The Mekong Delta offers drifting, cycling, and exploring experiences
verdicts.note: Chunk carries the article title 'Drift, cycle, explore: Vietnam's Mekong Delta'. Converting a headline into a factual claim is mildly generous, but the activities are asserted by the source. Counted correct, flagged as the most lenient of the six.

conclusion.reasoning: Approvals were 6/6 accurate; rejections were 4/6. The judge errs by rejecting claims a human would accept, never by rubber-stamping. So the true faithfulness is at or above the measured 87.0%.
conclusion.naive_correction: If ~1/3 of the 116 UNSUPPORTED verdicts are false rejections, ~38 claims flip to supported, giving roughly 91% rather than 87%.
conclusion.confidence_caveat: n=6 per direction is SMALL. A 2/6 error rate has very wide error bars -- the true rejection accuracy could plausibly sit anywhere from ~40% to ~90%. The DIRECTION of the bias (over-rejection, not rubber-stamping) is the trustworthy finding; the magnitude of the correction is not. Do not report 91% as a measured number.
